A1.justification: Both readable 11-page PDFs describe SURF and contain corresponding methods, equations, experiments, figures and tables. Neither includes appendix or supplementary pages; changes to referenced but unavailable supplementary material cannot be inferred.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original video-generation comparisons, runtime measurements, ablations and a preference study involving 37 researchers.

after.justification: V2 retains the original experiments, ablations and human-preference results in Tables 1–5 and Figures 5–8.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.3 retain the same noise-reshifting preview procedure, flow-mapping Refiner, degradation-based training and shifted-window attention. No algorithm or architecture change is documented.

E1.justification: Both use synthetic low/high-resolution training pairs and evaluation prompts from VBench, VideoPhy and PhyGenBench. The same 720p generation and 1080p refinement/super-resolution scenarios remain.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in Tables 1–3 and Figure 5 is unchanged, including reduced-step Wan, SVG, DMD and the four super-resolution baselines. Newly cited related works are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Both retain the same training schedule, metrics, runtime measurement procedure, 381-prompt evaluation, 100-sample 1080p comparison and 24-video/37-participant preference study.

E4.justification: Tables 4–5 retain the preview-step and Refiner-step ablations, and Figure 8 retains the shifted-window comparison. Deleting a pointer to supplementary quantitative results does not establish removal of an analysis contained in either PDF.

E5.justification: Both specify a fixed seed per evaluation prompt. Neither introduces repeated-run statistics, confidence intervals, error bars or significance testing.

E6.justification: Tables 1–5, Figure 5 preference rates and qualitative examples retain the same results. For example, Table 1 reports SURF quality score 83.26, runtime 278 seconds and 12.58× speedup in both versions.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and flow, noise-reshifting and shifted-attention equations (1)–(3) are unchanged. No theorem, proof or substantive derivation is added.

C1.justification: Both claim efficient high-resolution generation while preserving model signatures and compatibility with other acceleration methods. The abstract and conclusion retain the 12.5× Wan 2.1 and 8.7× HunyuanVideo speedup claims.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning signature preservation, layout stabilization near step 10, local-context sufficiency during refinement and baseline artifacts remain unchanged. No substantive limitation or applicability qualification is added.

D1.justification: Hardware, optimizer, learning rate, training schedule and project link remain unchanged. Section 4.1 drops a generic supplementary-configuration pointer, but Section 3.3 retains the supplementary architecture/training pointer; no concrete technical detail or code/data access change is established.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds DiTCtrl, Alchemist and Yang et al.'s RectifiedHR/energy-rectification work, modestly expanding related-work coverage. The two added Yang bibliography entries share arXiv:2503.02537 and represent the same work.

P1.justification: V2 removes Pengfei Wan from the author list, adds funding acknowledgements, deletes several supplementary-material pointers and bibliographic URL fields, and makes limited related-work wording edits. The overall narrative and section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds page-number footers, reflows text and references, and slightly reduces Figure 8's size. All eight figures and five tables retain their substantive visual content; no display is added or removed.

improvement.justification: V2 makes limited citation and presentation updates while retaining the same method, empirical support, technical disclosures and conclusions. Removing supplementary pointers supplies no missing evidence, and the added references include duplicate entries for one arXiv work. These edits produce no meaningful net difference in overall quality.
